# Every third-party jar on the desktop runtime classpath.
#
# Generated by `gradlew :desktop:auditDependencyNetworkSurface`. The build fails
# if this set changes, so a new dependency must be reviewed by a person before it
# can land -- including one containing no networking code.
#
# An earlier version of this file recorded ONLY jars containing networking code.
# That meant a new clean dependency produced an identical file and passed
# silently, so "the gate will catch it" was a false assurance for exactly the
# case a human should look at. Found by the design panel's platform reviewer,
# 2026-08-29.
#
# Jars flagged `[contains networking code]` reference a socket, URLConnection,
# HttpClient or NIO channel API somewhere in their bytecode. As measured on
# 2026-08-29 across 43 runtime jars -- Compose Multiplatform 1.9.0, Skiko,
# coroutines, the Kotlin stdlib -- that count is ZERO. The emptiness of that
# flag is a measurement, not an omission.
#
# The scanner is positive-controlled: run
#   gradlew :desktop:assertNoNetworkBytecode -PblanktickNetworkGateSelfTest
# and it must FAIL by finding NoNetwork.kt. If that passes, this file is noise.
